A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Activation Beacon, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. The shared method and experiments can be matched despite substantial revision. v1 has no appendix; v3's Appendices A and B are included in this comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, LongBench, topic-retrieval, efficiency and ablation results in Section 3.

after.justification: v3 reports original LongBench, needle-retrieval, multi-turn latency, short-context and ablation results for Llama-2 and Qwen-2 in Section 4.

M1.justification: The KV-compression principle remains, but v3 replaces end-appended beacons and customized attention masks with interleaved beacons and standard causal attention, changing within-chunk interactions. Its trainable module uses beacon-specific Q/K/V projections rather than v1's Q/K/V/O projections. Mixed-data training also becomes separate pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

E1.justification: LongBench remains, but PG19, Proof-Pile and CodeParrot language-modeling evaluations and topic retrieval disappear. v3 adds single- and multi-needle retrieval, multi-turn scenarios, MMLU, ARC-Challenge, BoolQ and GSM8K. Training coverage expands through BookSum and synthetic question answering over Books3 and arXiv material (Appendix A).

E2.justification: The LongBench comparison drops PI, NTK, StreamingLLM, YaRN, LongChat, LongAlpaca and LongLlama, adding Full-FT, ICAE, LongLLMLingua and SnapKV. The original Llama-2 baseline and AutoCompressor remain, but v3 additionally fine-tunes AutoCompressor and ICAE checkpoints on the same training data (v1 Table 3; v3 Section 4.1 and Table 1).

E3.justification: Training changes from 80K examples of up to 8K tokens to 1B-token pre-training followed by fine-tuning with contexts up to approximately 20K. Sampled training ratios narrow from 2–128 to 2–32. v3 adds Qwen-2-7B, switches Activation Beacon from SDPA to FlashAttention-2, and introduces multi-turn compression-plus-generation timing instead of the earlier forward-pass timing.

E4.justification: v3 retains the chunk-wise versus instance-wise sampling question, but revises attention and training ablations on Qwen-2, removes segmentation and fixed-ratio training controls, and separately ablates pre-training and fine-tuning (Table 4). Figure 5 adds inference-time sensitivity tests across compression ratios and context lengths, extending v1's training-strategy ablations.

E5.justification: v1 Table 4 specifies averages over 100 forward passes; v3 Section 4.3 specifies 20 repetitions with distinct needle positions for the new multi-turn experiment. These concern different protocols, not a comparable reduction in run count. Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: LongBench results are replaced under revised training: Llama-2 single-document QA is 27.14 in v1 Table 3 and 34.9 in v3 Table 1, which does not establish a same-setting gain. Earlier perplexity, topic-retrieval and training-cost results disappear. New results include retrieval and short-context scores, and Qwen-2 third-turn latency of 2.981 seconds versus Full-FT's 6.153 seconds (v3 Table 2).

T1.justification: v3 adds a limited formal FLOPs derivation separating attention and other computation (Equations 9–10 and Appendix B), beyond v1's qualitative efficiency discussion. Its Equation 11 also omits the negative-log term present in v1 Equation 4, leaving the written minimization inconsistent with the stated next-token training objective.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from extending Llama-2's context from 4K to 400K with inexpensive short-sequence training to effective, efficient and flexible long-context compression. v3 emphasizes comparable accuracy to an uncompressed fine-tuned baseline, approximately 2x faster inference and 8x KV-cache reduction across Llama-2 and Qwen-2, replacing the earlier 100x-extension and nine-hour-training headline claims.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes separating context-extension benefits from baseline weight updates. v3 develops explanations involving soft-token bottlenecks, query-independent cache reuse across turns and SnapKV's failure beyond its native window. It recommends 8x compression and acknowledges small short-context performance losses, qualifying v1's assurance of complete preservation.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds document filtering, synthetic-QA construction, conversation formatting, a prompt template and replay-data details. v3 also documents stage-specific learning rates, loss masking and gradient propagation. The abstract changes a promised model/code release to a reported data/model/code release. Conversely, v1's explicit training-step and wall-clock accounting is absent for the revised training recipe.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions the work against context-compression methods, adding discussion of ICAE, LongLLMLingua, SnapKV and CCM, alongside KV-compression approaches including CLA, GQA, MLA and KIVI. Much of v1's context-extension and external-memory retrieval positioning is removed or condensed. This changes the substantive novelty argument.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology and conclusion are extensively rewritten around compression. Related work moves before the method, and experiments are reorganized around effectiveness, efficiency, flexibility, short-context capabilities and ablations. Terminology shifts from condensing intervals to compression chunks, with substantially expanded procedural explanations.

P2.justification: The mechanism diagrams are redrawn to show interleaving, and LongBench and ablation tables are restructured. Earlier perplexity, topic-retrieval and efficiency displays are replaced by FLOPs curves, needle-retrieval heatmaps, compression-ratio plots and multi-turn/short-context tables. Appendix A also adds a boxed conversation template.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation through comparisons using the same training data, two evaluated backbones, direct long-context retrieval tests and empirical checks of short-context preservation. These address important weaknesses in v1's controls and largely asserted preservation claim; Appendix A also improves reproducibility. The gains outweigh the removal of language-modeling and training-cost studies, although the apparent loss-formula error in Equation 11 remains a quality defect.
